```text
pkg/spi/fence.go:23:func CodeFence(lang, content string) string {
func CodeFence(lang, content string) string {
	fence := strings.Repeat("`", fenceLen(content))
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s%s\n%s\n%s", fence, lang, content, fence)
}

// fenceLen returns the fence length needed to safely wrap content: at least 3,
// and always strictly greater than the longest run of consecutive backticks in
// content, so no line inside content can act as a closing fence.
func fenceLen(content string) int {
	longest, run := 0, 0
	for _, r := range content {
		if r == '`' {
			run++
			if run > longest {
				longest = run
			}
		} else {
			run = 0
		}
	}
	if n := longest + 1; n > 3 {
		return n
	}
	return 3
}

// CapRunes truncates s to at most max runes, marking the cut. Rune-based so a
// cap never splits a multi-byte character. Scans rune boundaries instead of
// converting to []rune, which would allocate O(len(s)) for exactly the
// oversized tool results this cap protects against.
func CapRunes(s string, max int) string {
	if len(s) <= max {
		return s // fast path: byte length bounds rune length
	}
	count := 0
	for i := range s {
		if count == max {
			return s[:i] + "\n… (output truncated)"
		}
		count++
	}
```

```text
## v2.14.0 2026-09-22

### 📢 Announcements

- The SpecStory CLI now supports [Grok Build](https://x.ai/cli) (i.e. `grok`, `agent`), SpaceXAI's terminal coding agent, for sessions created from Grok Build version `1.0.34` or higher. Sessions from earlier versions may work, but are not officially supported. This provides the same support for saving to local markdown files and to the SpecStory Cloud as for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/docs/api/claude-code), [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/docs/cli), [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/), Factory's [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli), [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/product), Google's [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/), [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI), [VS Code Copilot](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/copilot), [Muse Code](https://developer.meta.com/ai/products/muse-code/), [Pi](https://pi.dev) and [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code).
- Grok is a cross-provider `specstory resume` target: you can resume any agent's session into Grok, and resume a Grok session into another agent.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Bare `specstory run` launches Claude Code as documented, rather than choosing the first provider alphabetically. The help text and configured command now use the same default.
- Muse Code sessions containing a single JSONL line larger than the 64MB limit now render with that line skipped, instead of failing to render the whole session.
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-1 2026-09-22 18:41:50Z)**_

The backtick change is expected, and it comes from a 2.13.0 change that this repo had not been re-synced with yet. Nothing in 2.14.0 itself touched fence rendering.

**Why the fences grew**

The tool-result fence for Claude Code output is now sized dynamically. The helper at `pkg/spi/fence.go:23` scans the content for the longest run of backticks and emits a fence one longer than that, with a minimum of three. Every hunk you're seeing is a Read or Bash result whose content itself contains a triple-backtick run. In the first file, for example, the Read of a session-data JSON file includes markdown strings with embedded ``` fences, so the wrapper became ````. That is what stops a fence inside the content from prematurely closing the block and wrecking everything rendered after it.

**Why it shows up now**

- The generic dynamic fence helper was added on 2026-08-07 and shipped in v2.8.0. That commit did not touch the Claude Code tool-result path, which still hard-coded ```` ```text ````.
- The Claude Code tool-result path was switched to the dynamic helper on 2026-09-16 in the "minor code cleanup to bring providers into more symmetry" commit. That shipped in v2.13.0 on 2026-09-17. The v2.13.0 changelog notes it: "Remaining cases where embedded code fences could break transcript formatting are also fixed for Claude Code, Droid, and DeepSeek TUI tool output."
- Your history files were last committed on 2026-08-12, and this appears to be the first sync of this repo with a 2.13-or-later build. So the diff is the one-time rewrite the earlier v2.8.0 changelog warned about, just arriving late for the Claude Code sessions.

**What else is in the diff**

Of the 94 modified files, 88 contain nothing but fence resizing. The other six have real content changes, also from 2.13.0:

- Three Codex sessions from 2026-09-15 lost the "Input (truncated)" cutoff, which is the Codex custom-tool input fix in the 2.13.0 changelog.
- Three Pi sessions from July switched from a compact inline path to labeled `**Path:** / **Offset (line):** / **Limit:**` fields. That comes from the Pi provider completion commit on 2026-09-17, also in v2.13.0. It is the largest source of added lines because Pi Read results now also render the offset and limit inputs.

One thing worth a look: in those Pi files, the Read result's content fence is still a bare ```` ``` ```` immediately after the labeled fields, while the Claude Code path now uses the dynamic helper. If a Pi Read returns markdown containing fences, that block can still break, so the Pi renderer may deserve the same treatment.

```text
   112	func renderToolOutput(tool *schema.ToolInfo, success bool) string {
   113		var blocks []string
   114		var consumed []string
   115		name := strings.ToLower(tool.Name)
   116		if content, ok := tool.Output["content"].(string); ok {
   117			lang := "text"
   118			if success && name == "read" {
   119				lang = spi.LanguageFromPath(spi.StringValue(tool.Input, "path"))
   120			}
   121			if name == "bash" || name == "powershell" {
   122				content = sanitizeShellOutput(content)
   123			}
   124			if content != "" {
   125				blocks = append(blocks, spi.CodeFence(lang, spi.CapRunes(content, 5000)))
   126			}
   127			consumed = append(consumed, "content")
   128		}
   129		if success && name == "edit" {
   130			if details, ok := tool.Output["details"].(map[string]any); ok {
   131				var rendered []string
   132				for _, key := range []string{"diff", "patch"} {
   133					if diff, ok := details[key].(string); ok {
   134						blocks = append(blocks, "**"+key+":**\n"+spi.CodeFence("diff", spi.CapRunes(diff, 5000)))
   135						rendered = append(rendered, key)
   136					}
   137				}
   138				if extra := cappedToolJSON(details, rendered...); extra != "" {
   139					blocks = append(blocks, "**Details:**\n"+extra)
   140				}
   141				consumed = append(consumed, "details")
   142			}
   143		}
   144		if _, ok := tool.Output["is_error"].(bool); ok {
   145			consumed = append(consumed, "is_error")
   146		}
   147		if extra := cappedToolJSON(tool.Output, consumed...); extra != "" {
   148			blocks = append(blocks, extra)
   149		}
   150		return strings.Join(blocks, "\n\n")
   151	}
   152	
   153	// Cap JSON before fencing it so truncation cannot remove the closing fence.
   154	func cappedToolJSON(values map[string]any, drop ...string) string {
   155		kept := make(map[string]any, len(values))
   156		for key, value := range values {
   157			kept[key] = value
   158		}
   159		for _, key := range drop {
   160			delete(kept, key)
   161		}
   162		if len(kept) == 0 {
   163			return ""
   164		}
   165		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(kept, "", "  ")
   166		if err != nil {
   167			return ""
   168		}
   169		return spi.CodeFence("json", spi.CapRunes(string(data), 5000))
   170	}
   171	
   172	func sanitizeShellOutput(content string) string {
   173		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r\n", "\n")
   174		return strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
   175			if unicode.IsControl(r) && r != '\n' && r != '\t' {
   176				return -1
   177			}
   178			return r
   179		}, ansi.Strip(content))
   180	}
```

````text
// FormatDiffBlock renders a before/after pair as a diff-fenced block, marking
// every old line with "-" and every new line with "+". Either side may be empty
// (a file creation or deletion), in which case only the other side is emitted.
func FormatDiffBlock(oldText, newText string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	if oldText != "" {
		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(oldText, "\n") {
			b.WriteString("-")
			b.WriteString(line)
			b.WriteString("\n")
		}
	}
	if newText != "" {
		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(newText, "\n") {
			b.WriteString("+")
			b.WriteString(line)
			b.WriteString("\n")
		}
	}
	return CodeFence("diff", strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n"))
}

// RenderGenericJSON is the fallback renderer for a tool whose arguments have no
// bespoke layout: it shows the raw arguments as pretty-printed JSON rather than
// guessing at a shape. Keys named in dropKeys are omitted, which lets a provider
// hide labels its agent injects into every call; when nothing survives the drop
// there is nothing worth showing and the result is "".
func RenderGenericJSON(args map[string]any, dropKeys ...string) string {
	kept := make(map[string]any, len(args))
	for key, val := range args {
		if slices.Contains(dropKeys, key) {
			continue
		}
		kept[key] = val
	}
	if len(kept) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	// MarshalIndent sorts map keys, so the fallback is deterministic. Arguments
	// come from json.Unmarshal, so re-marshaling them cannot realistically fail;
	// an error still yields "" rather than a half-rendered block.
	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(kept, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	return CodeFence("json", string(data))
}

// sessionMarkdown returns the session as markdown for the preview — the real specstory
// render when the session can be re-parsed (needs a cwd), else the plain FTS body.
func sessionMarkdown(registry *factory.Registry, store *sessionindex.Store, s *sessionindex.Session) string {
	if s.OriginCwd != "" {
		if prov, err := registry.Get(s.Agent); err == nil {
			if full, err := prov.GetAgentChatSession(s.OriginCwd, s.SessionID, false); err == nil &&
				full != nil && full.SessionData != nil {
				if md, err := session.GenerateMarkdownFromAgentSession(full.SessionData, false, true); err == nil {
					return md
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if body, _ := store.SessionBody(s.Agent, s.SessionID); strings.TrimSpace(body) != "" {
		return "```\n" + body + "\n```"
	}
	return "_(no readable content for this session)_"
}
````
